title: Region-aware circuit orchestration for Redis/Kafka/DB with progressive load-shedding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our inference API surfaces tail errors and elevated latencies when downstream stores (Redis cache, Kafka ingestion, primary DB) degrade in a single region. This manifests as client timeouts, connection pool exhaustion, and region failover storms. Existing approaches are ad-hoc: per-service circuit breakers or simple retries that either over-react (mass failed requests) or under-react (slow requests pile up).

Goal: Implement a coordinated, region-aware circuit orchestration layer plus progressive load-shedding strategies for Redis, Kafka, and DB dependencies to preserve global SLOs during partial degradation and reduce blast radius during failover. The solution should be deployable for Hosted and Dedicated tiers and be compatible with Private deployments (control-plane flags only). Success criteria: (1) keep global 99th percentile request latency within SLO during single-region cache or DB degradation for 95% of injected failures, (2) reduce connection pool exhaustion incidents by 80% in chaos tests, (3) provide clear observability and an operator runbook.

Scope: design, implementation, tests (chaos/bench), dashboards/alerts, rollout, and runbook. Not covered: deep re-architecture of KV store clients; that is follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Circuit orchestration component deployed behind feature flag in staging and can open/close per-dependency per-region. 2) Progressive shedding policies (cache-first, consumer-lag-based for Kafka, write-defer for DB) implemented and toggled with percentage knobs. 3) Dashboards show expected metrics and alert on budget burn. 4) Runbook tested end-to-end with injected Redis latency and simulated regional outage.
design_decision_summary:
We will implement a lightweight control-plane orchestrator (stateless API) that collects per-region dependency health signals and publishes region-aware decisions to sidecars running next to service instances. Sidecars enforce local circuit state and shedding rules. Key decisions:

- Signal sources: connection pool exhaustion, 95/99 latency, error rate, Kafka consumer lag, and Redis miss spike. Signals will be aggregated per-region with a short TTL window (30s) to avoid flapping.
- Circuit model: three-tiered states: CLOSED, PROBING, OPEN. PROBING allows a small percentage of traffic through for health checks and for re-evaluating capacity.
- Progressive shedding: a policy pipeline ordered by impact: first degrade non-critical caches (stale-while-revalidate), next reduce background ingestion and non-user-critical tooling, next impose per-tenant request-rate limits and graceful degradation to static fallbacks. Critical writes to DB are queue-with-backoff with local durable drop when safe.
- Multi-region failover coordination: control-plane will mark a region as degraded and move non-stateful traffic to healthy regions subject to capacity quotas. Stateful traffic with affinity will be degraded rather than failed over automatically unless operator enables cross-region failover.
- Connection pooling: sidecar exposes dynamic pool size hints to clients and will return circuit hints for per-client connections (e.g., mark connections as "discouraged to take new work"). We avoid hard-coded global pool changes; instead we provide gradual shrink/growth signals to allow graceful drain.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized decisions vs fully local heuristics: centralization gives global view to avoid thundering herd, but introduces a control-plane dependency. We mitigate by making sidecars default to safe local fallback if control-plane unreachable.
- Strict failover vs degrade-first: strict failover can recover latency but risks violating data locality/consistency. We prefer degrade-first, with opt-in cross-region failover for enterprise customers.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged implementation behind control-plane toggle. 2) Canary: enable for internal-only services in eu-central-1 with conservative thresholds. 3) Run 72-hour chaos experiment: inject 2x latency and 50% error-rate into Redis in eu-central-1 and verify global SLOs. 4) Gradually expand to other internal services and then to beta customers in controlled waves. 5) After 2 weeks of stable operation, flip on for all hosted API traffic for non-enterprise customers with monitoring alarms. 6) Offer cross-region failover switch as an enterprise opt-in in Dedicated/Private with an additional safety gate (manual approval).
telemetry_and_alerts:
Primary metrics we will emit and dashboard:
- dep.redis.region.p50_latency_ms, dep.redis.region.p95_latency_ms, dep.redis.region.error_rate
- dep.kafka.consumer_lag, dep.kafka.ingest_rate, dep.kafka.region.error_rate
- dep.db.max_connections, dep.db.wait_count, dep.db.region.p95_latency_ms
- connpool.wait_seconds, connpool.active_connections, connpool.max_configured
- circuit.orchestrator.region.state, circuit.orchestrator.open_count, shedding.rate

Example alert rules (Grafana/Prometheus):
- Critical: if dep.db.max_connections / dep.db.max_configured > 0.9 for 3m and connection wait_count > 100 -> Pager
- High: if dep.redis.region.p95_latency_ms > 500ms for 5m and error_rate > 1% -> On-call
- SLO burn: if request_error_budget_burn_rate > 5x for 30m -> Pager

Sample PromQL snippets we will add to dashboards:
- Redis p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redis_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
- Connpool waiters: sum(rate(connpool_wait_seconds_count[1m])) by (service, region)
- Circuit open ratio: sum(circuit_state == 2) / count(circuit_state) by (region)

All metrics will carry region and dependency tags. We will add a dedicated "degradation session" timeline showing control-plane decisions, sidecar confirmations, and affected tenant list.
runbook:
Operator steps for a degraded Redis region:
1) SRE alert triggers: check orchestrator dashboard and 'degradation session' timeline. 2) Confirm control-plane decision: does orchestrator show region state=OPEN? 3) If region OPEN: check affected tenants and ensure canary traffic is diverted. 4) If there is increased db.wait_count, reduce global write rate by toggling write-rate limiter via console and enable write-queue for best-effort writes. 5) For Kafka ingestion backpressure, temporarily drop non-critical topics and scale consumer groups in healthy regions. 6) To restore: move orchestrator to PROBING, monitor small traffic through for 2m, then to CLOSED when p95/p99 metrics back within thresholds for 10m. 7) Post-incident: run postmortem and check evaluated thresholds—tune percent tolerances and probe window.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for sidecar decision enforcement and circuit state transitions. 2) Staging integration: simulated Redis/Kafka/DB degradation tests verifying sidecars respect shed percentages and queues. 3) Chaos: use litmus/chaos-engine to inject latency, packet loss, and connection termination in a single region while measuring global p99, error budget burn, and connpool saturation. 4) Load tests to find safe capacity quotas for cross-region shift and to validate gradual pool shrink heuristics.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: control-plane becomes a single point of failure. Mitigation: sidecars default to conservative local heuristics and cache last-known decisions for short TTLs. Risk: aggressive shedding may silently drop customer data. Mitigation: tiered shedding policy with explicit labels for data-critical flows and blocking automatic drop unless operator-approved. Risk: noisy metrics cause flapping. Mitigation: use 30s aggregation window and hysteresis (min-open-time 60s).
